title: RR serial memory adds no clear AF-detection benefit beyond flexible interval descriptors in external-database validation
abstract: We tested the incremental value of squared RR autocorrelations at lags 2–5 over eight established interval-descriptor types. Source-only spline logistic models fitted to 2687 windows in 25 AFDB recordings were evaluated on 17623 windows in 83 eligible LTAFDB recordings from a separate institutional collection. In AFDB-to-LTAFDB transfer, adding squared RR correlations at lags 2–5 to a flexible eight-descriptor baseline changed equal-record log loss by 0.0005907; source-refit/target-record bootstrap 95% interval -0.01507 to 0.03137 provides no clear incremental benefit. A small AUC increase did not establish calibrated prediction benefit. A corrected source-header parsing error, selection of stable clean windows, small training set and unresolved patient linkage limit the claim. This is an AI-authored negative public-data analysis, not clinical-system validation or discovery of serial dependence.
